title: RADIOISOTOPE THERMOELECTRIC GENERATOR THERMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a passive thermal system to regulate the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator temperature and to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system.Description: For exploration missions, there is a need (In situ resource utilization, deep space missions, long night survival...) to use efficient power generation systems as an alternative to solar panels. Europe is already engaged in developing a Radioisotope Heater Unit (RHU) and the next step is to develop bigger capabilities witha Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG). As RTG is generating significant waste heat, there is an interest to reuse this heatand optimize the thermal control system, hence the whole system. Several thermal management systems with heat recovery are currently under study with the potential capability of receiving waste heat form RHU or RTG. However, interfacing with an RTG and regulatingits temperature is complex and requires a dedicated system for this unit. The goal of the activity is to develop a passive thermal system that regulates the temperature of the RTG and be able to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system viaa dedicated thermal interface. The RTG thermal system requires to operate with less than 5% of the electrical power generated bytheRTG. The heat recovery and the distribution of the RTG thermal energy would increase the overall efficiency of the system by more than 20%. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation - Technology trade off review - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator - Way forward for industrializationDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: PHASE A SPACE BASED RE-ENTRY MONITOR - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure from orbit the destructive re-entry of artificial space objects in the Earth's atmosphere by means of a dedicated set of sensors. Pre-cursor sensor level activities haveidentified AlO (aluminium oxide band and associate lithium markers) and SWIR (shortwave infrared) as the most promising and accessible wavelengths from orbit that most re-entry events of artificial will have in common. The study shall establish the system level accommodation of such a sensor suite on a large CubeSat or small satellite platform with capable AOCS suite for pointing and orbit control.As uncontrolled or controlled re-entry events can occur anywhere on the globe, it is envisaged the satelliteplatform shall be in a relatively high orbit to ensure the field of view of the sensors can point to the re-entry streaks generated(which can last for 100'sof km) and preferential observation geometries (such as re-entry event in the Earth shadow) can be reached on average for 1 out of the on average 3 re-entries daily within the forecasting period of a ground segment (roughly two days prior to the event). The mobility needs of the platform shall thus be an integral part of the phase A level tradeoffs.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, theorbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need on regularly observing re-entry events. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. hyperspectral cameras and SWIR imagers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirementsto be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, andassessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: PHASE A SAMPLING THE NEUTRAL DENSITY OF THE LOWER THERMOSPHERE - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure in-situ the neutral density, and when feasible the ion density as well, in very low-Earth orbit, i.e. the lower thermosphere below 250km and if feasiblebelow 200km, from aneccentric orbit with high inclination. The eccentricity shall be tuned to ensure orbital lifetimes spanning a significant part of the solar cycle and the high inclination shall ensure the capture of samples across the dynamic atmospheric regions that affect the majority of current spacecraft and can support the new generation of VLEO satellites.To couple in-situ measurements that can be used to calibrate atmosphere models in the region of interest with space safety applications such as improved orbital lifetime estimation of collision avoidance risk assessment, direct coupling with the mission dragprofiles is needed. Therefore, the mission shall embark an accelerometer and optimise its shape and AOCS control to facilitate precise orbit determination.Very low perigee orbits, with apogee still in low Earth orbit, are a challenge for space surveillance and tracking systems due to limited visibility from individual sensors and the orbit being highly affected by drag. The mission shall function as a calibration target for commercial tracking solution in Europe, to demonstrate the accuracy of their products against a ground truth provide by the mission in support of safely operating in the VLEO regime.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, the orbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need of performing orbital lifetime calculation and collision avoidance processes below 300km. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. mass spectrometers, accelerometers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Given the eccentric orbit crossing highly utilised space traffic reason, perform a trade-off in platform manoeuvrability needs to extend the mission duration while managing collusion risk in accordance with ESA's space debris mitigation requirements. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirements to be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, and assessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.
